backdown tag

Tags: facts about content — person, place, kind, event, date. Create them and attach them to content, people or places.

On this page

  • backdown tag rm
  • Options

backdown tag [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

backdown tag add#

Create a tag (or find the matching one), and optionally attach it to a target.

backdown tag add [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> --value <VALUE>

Options#

--kind <KIND>
What it is about: owner, kind, location, country, city, place, airport, event, date, memory.
--value <VALUE>
Its value, e.g. "Hong Kong" or "HKG".
--parent <PARENT>
A parent tag id, for a hierarchy (a city under its country).
--data <DATA>
Extra data as JSON (coordinates, codes).
--to <TARGET>
Attach it to this target: content:<sha256hex>, subject:<key>, entity:<key> or path:<key>.
--source <SOURCE>
Where the tag came from. Default: user.
--confidence <CONFIDENCE>
How sure, 0..1. Default: 1.

backdown tag rm#

Remove a tag from a target.

backdown tag rm [OPTIONS] --tag <TAG> --from <TARGET>

Options#

--tag <TAG>
The tag id (backdown tag list).
--from <TARGET>
The target to remove it from.

backdown tag list#

List tags, optionally of one kind.

backdown tag list [OPTIONS]

Options#

--kind <KIND>
&nbsp;
--json
Print it as JSON, for scripts.

backdown tag of#

Show the tags a target carries.

backdown tag of [OPTIONS] <TARGET>

Arguments#

<TARGET>
content:<sha256hex>, subject:<key>, entity:<key> or path:<key>.

Options#

--json
Print it as JSON, for scripts.

backdown tag exif#

Read a photo or video's own metadata (EXIF / QuickTime) and attach date and location tags.

backdown tag exif [OPTIONS] <PATHS>...

Arguments#

<PATHS>...
The files to read, or folders: every indexed photo and video under them (each must be indexed; one backdown hash hasn't read is hashed now).

Options#

--geo
Also tag the country, region, city and nearest airport of each position, as tag geo does.
--again
In folders, read again what was read before (named files always are).
--source <SOURCE>
Where the derived tags are recorded as coming from. Default: exif.

backdown tag find#

Find content by where it was taken and what it's tagged with: everything within a distance of a place, carrying tags, taken between dates.

backdown tag find [OPTIONS]

Options#

--near <PLACE>
Around a place: an airport's code (HKG), a town or city (Paris, or "Paris, Texas"), or a position (22.3089,113.9146).
--km <KM>
How far from it, in km. Default: 120.
--tag <KIND=VALUE>
A tag it must carry: KIND=VALUE (airport=HKG, country=Hong Kong, event=Boat show 2019) or a tag id from tag list. Repeat it for more; all must be there.
--from <DATE>
Taken on or after: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.
--to <DATE>
Taken on or before: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.
--sort <SORT>
nearest (the default around a place), newest (otherwise) or oldest.
--limit <LIMIT>
Show at most this many (0: all of them). Default: 0.
--paths
Print only the path of every copy, one per line, for scripts (| xargs …).
--json
Print it as JSON, for scripts.

backdown tag geo#

Derive country, region, city and nearest-airport tags from the location tags already on content (attach those first with tag exif). Offline, from embedded reference data.

backdown tag geo [OPTIONS] [TARGETS]...

Arguments#

[TARGETS]...
Limit to these content items (content:<sha256hex>); with none, every located item.

Options#

--source <SOURCE>
Where the derived tags are recorded as coming from. Default: geo.
--about
Print the embedded dataset sizes and data attribution, then exit.

All of them also take the global options --db and --local.

Examples#

# read the dates and positions of every indexed photo and video under a folder, and name their places
backdown tag exif ~/Pictures --geo
# everything within 120 km of Hong Kong's airport, nearest first
backdown tag find --near HKG
# a town (the most populous of that name, or say which), closer in, in one year
backdown tag find --near "Paris, France" --km 20 --from 2019 --to 2019
# by tags: all of them must be there
backdown tag find --tag country="Hong Kong" --tag event="Boat show 2019"
# just the paths, for other tools
backdown tag find --near 22.3089,113.9146 --km 5 --paths | xargs -d '\n' ls -l
backdown tag add --kind event --value "Boat show 2019" --to content:<sha256>
